perspective:
**Available to Alice Lim**

- Alice knows she is a dental hygienist. She knows Austin Moreno as her old friend from high school; they have stayed close, discuss their personal/professional lives, and support each other. She knows his work context as an insurance/office job.
- She has observed Austin acting reserved when they talk about work. This makes her believe he may be hiding something about his job performance. She feels concerned and curious.
- **Coffee conversation:** Alice invited Austin to coffee. She asked if everything was okay at the office and encouraged him to talk. She heard Austin say it was “nothing really,” just “usual ups and downs,” then that he wasn’t sure how to handle a few things at work and it was complicated.
- After this, Alice believes Austin might be considering a career change because of dissatisfaction at work. She feels worried and shares her own healthcare experience. She asks if he has thought about changing careers, suggests healthcare, and offers to explain more and connect him with contacts. She hears Austin say he has thought about it but doesn’t know what path; he finds healthcare interesting and wants to know more.
- Alice senses Austin is hesitant about changing careers due to fear of the unknown. She feels frustration and empathy. She tells him career changes are daunting but possible, shares that her friend Lara switched to healthcare in her late 30s and is happier, and encourages stepping out of comfort zones while offering support. She hears Austin say it is inspiring but risky, and that her support and real success stories help.
- Seeing Austin’s openness, Alice feels encouraged and hopeful. She offers to connect him with a career counselor and friends in healthcare, says it is about taking first steps, and says she will set up a meeting next week. She hears Austin accept, appreciate the connections, and say he looks forward to it.
- After several discussions and meetings, Alice believes Austin is ready to take next steps and appreciates her help. She feels satisfaction and joy and plans regular check-ins. She tells Austin she is proud of his steps and asks how he feels. She hears him say he feels excited, nervous, and mostly grateful. She suggests regular check-ins; Austin agrees, saying it will keep him focused and he values her perspective.
- Alice does not have access to Austin’s private thoughts or unspoken facts. Her conclusions about his dissatisfaction, possible career change, hesitation, and readiness are her own observations/beliefs unless Austin stated them to her.
